_rationale._scope: Lints the CMS CSS ONLY - orkui/template/default/frontdoor/css/*.css + orkui/template/default/cms/css/*.css (7 files). The CRM's orkui/template/default/style/** is in .stylelintignore on purpose: it is mixed tabs/spaces with ~78 !important each, and linting it would mean a repo-wide reformat nobody asked for. The CMS gets to hold a stricter standard than the CRM.
_rationale._indentation: stylelint REMOVED the 'indentation' rule in v16 (deprecated in 15, dropped in 16 - verified against the installed 16.26.1: node_modules/stylelint/lib/rules/ has no 'indentation' entry). It is therefore NOT configured. 4-space indent is enforced instead by the 'lint:css:tabs' npm script, an awk tab guard that fails if any line in a CMS CSS file starts with a tab; 'npm run lint:css' runs stylelint AND that guard.
_rationale.no-descending-specificity: off - the light-rules-then-dark-rules structure (html[data-theme=dark] blocks after their light partners) trips this everywhere with no defect behind it.
_rationale.selector-class-pattern: off - the CMS uses short prefixed classes (.pe-card, .te-select, .fd-btn-gold) that no single kebab pattern usefully describes.
_rationale.selector-id-pattern: off - 18 hits, all of them IDs this CSS does not own and cannot rename: #theme_container is emitted by default.theme (ORK shell) and #cmsAddModal by a CMS template. Pure noise.
_rationale.keyframes-name-pattern: off - the CMS names keyframes in camelCase (fdRModalIn, cmsErrFlash). Not autofixable, and renaming means hand-editing every animation: reference for a cosmetic gain.
_rationale.declaration-block-no-redundant-longhand-: off - collapsing longhands to shorthand changes which properties a later rule can override; not worth the cascade risk for zero visual gain.
_rationale.declaration-block-single-line-max-declar: off - 269 hits and NOT autofixable (meta.fixable is false on 16.26.1), so it means 269 hand whitespace edits. Compact single-line rules for one-off overrides are the deliberate house style in blocks.css/cms-admin.css/blog.css. No defect behind any of them.
_rationale.alpha-value-notation: off - would rewrite hundreds of existing rgba(..., .4) values for zero benefit.
_rationale.color-function-notation: off - same: a mass rewrite of legacy comma-separated rgba() for zero benefit.
_rationale.media-feature-range-notation: prefix - keeps the existing (max-width: 900px) syntax rather than rewriting every query to range notation.
_rationale.shorthand-property-no-redundant-values: off - redundant-looking shorthands are written deliberately in places to mirror an adjacent rule; churn with no defect.
_rationale.comment-empty-line-before: off - the CMS files use dense annotated blocks where a blank line before every comment would double the file height.
_rationale.declaration-empty-line-before: off - same, applied to custom-property blocks.
_rationale.rule-empty-line-before: off - same; the token blocks list many one-line rules intentionally packed.
_rationale.value-keyword-case: off - would rewrite vendor/legacy value casing with no defect behind it.
_rationale.property-no-vendor-prefix: off - and this one is a CORRECTNESS reason, not a taste one. The rule IS autofixable, and its fix DELETES the prefixed declaration. All three hits are prefixes Safari/iOS still require: -webkit-backdrop-filter (Safari has no unprefixed backdrop-filter), -webkit-mask-image, and -webkit-text-size-adjust (iOS). Leaving the rule on would let --fix silently regress Safari.
_rationale.selector-not-notation: off - also a correctness reason. The rule IS autofixable and would rewrite :not(.fd-nav):not(.org-footer) to :not(.fd-nav, .org-footer). Those are NOT equivalent: chained :not() contributes one class of specificity per link (0,2,0) while the selector-list form contributes only its most specific argument (0,1,0). The autofix would silently drop specificity and change the cascade.
